STRONG SINGLE PROMPT arm. One prompt carrying the full guidelines text, the published criteria and weights, the org record and all 11 non-meta ledger items, plus explicit grounding rules, the 1,200-word hard limit, the verbatim section headings, the budget/overhead constraints and a plain-English style brief. No analyze stage, no org research, no voice stage, no strategy reservation, no design object, no validation loop, no claim ledger. Output taken exactly as returned - not edited, not shortened, not repaired.

CALLS = 2, and BOTH ARE BILLED. The first call (max_tokens 7000, reasoning_effort medium, gen-1787780036-JSrNbng76XBC9YO0wpR6) returned finish_reason=length: 6,719 of its 6,996 completion tokens went to reasoning and it truncated mid-sentence inside Q1, producing no usable proposal. It was retried once with max_tokens 14000 and reasoning_effort low (gen-1787780125-mqmvOOcn7kQLyZNE8Lvf), which completed with finish_reason=stop and 0 reasoning tokens. The retry was a capacity retry on a truncated call, not a quality retry - the prompt text was byte-identical between the two calls and no feedback from the first attempt was fed into the second. Costs and tokens above are the sum of both; the second call alone was $0.00741, 3,038 prompt / 3,343 completion.

WORD COUNT - THIS ARM FAILS THE HARD LIMIT. All counts are wc -w, never model-estimated. Whole file including the 46-word synthetic-fixture HTML comment: 2,253. Proposal text with that label stripped (the figure reported in word_count, matching the arm A convention): 2,207. Donor-countable length, i.e. the five answers with the level-2 headings, the budget table and the declaration all excluded exactly as the call's own rule excludes them: 1,760 words against a 1,200 hard limit. That is 560 words over, 47 per cent over. Under the funder's stated rule the application is returned unread and cannot be resubmitted in the round, so on the call's own terms this submission scores zero regardless of content. The prompt stated the limit twice, gave a target band of 1,120-1,200 words and warned that over 1,200 the application is returned unread; the model overshot anyway. Compare arm A (pipeline) at 1,103 donor-countable words, which was inside the limit - arm A has a deterministic length check and a shorten repair pass, this arm has neither, and that is precisely the difference the ladder is measuring.

ARITHMETIC - verified by hand, all correct. Budget direct costs 36,000 + 16,500 + 4,200 + 3,600 + 1,800 + 1,400 = 63,500, stated as 63,500. Overhead 7,000 = 11.02 per cent of 63,500, under the 12 per cent cap and shown as a single separate line. Total 70,500, inside the 25,000-75,000 band, over 18 months, inside the 18-month ceiling. Q4 destinations 24 + 9 + 6 = 39, matching the stated 39. 57/72 = 79.2 per cent, stated 79. 30/39 = 76.9 per cent, stated 77. 30/72 = 41.7 per cent, stated 'under 42 per cent'. 50 completers of 72 is a 30.6 per cent drop-out, stated as 'exceeds 30 per cent'. Nothing here required a checker to catch.

GROUNDING - one unsupported causal claim, otherwise clean. Q2 cause 1 states '9 did not complete enrolment because they lacked continuous transition casework' and frames it as 'our 2024-25 referral data proves this gap'. The 9 is sound arithmetic from E-WEB-2 (27 referred minus 18 enrolled), but the stated reason for the shortfall is nowhere in the ledger and is asserted as proven rather than as a hypothesis. A claim ledger would classify this as unsupported and material; this arm has no claim ledger, so it went out. Everything else traces: Kelverton, 41,000, CIO 2016, six staff / 4.2 FTE, ~25 volunteers, GBP 214,000, two years of accounts, three evenings a week, Marlpit, east bank, 38 per cent lowest income decile at the 2021 census, Dunmore Sixth Form College one mile away, 27 referred / 18 enrolled in 2024-25, Second Chances Jan-Apr 2025 with 24 started / 19 finished / 11 progressed. No invented staff names, trustee names, street names, employers, second ward or extra funders; unnamed future destinations are correctly written as commitments to identify rather than as existing partners. 'Over the past decade' (Q1) is a slight stretch for an organisation constituted in 2016 in 2026, but it is not a new fact.

OTHER OBSERVED DEFECTS. Two US spellings ('organizational' twice, 'enroll' once) despite an explicit British-English instruction. Q3 gives each cohort 20 weeks of phases inside a 6-month slot, which is consistent but never reconciled. 'Progression Gateway' is a name the model coined for the continuing practice; it is a label for a plan, not a claim of an existing thing, so it is not a grounding breach, but it is unattributed branding. The three Round 3 priorities are all addressed and the Q4 'what would count as this not having worked' question, which the prompt flagged as usually dodged, is answered with real thresholds.

FIXTURE. Halewater Commons Trust, Kelverton, Marlpit, Dunmore Sixth Form College, the Wren Hill Foundation and the Neighbourhood Futures Fund are all synthetic and do not exist. out-n03-C.md carries the synthetic label as its first line, as a 46-word HTML comment that a markdown reader does not render; it is not part of the proposal and is excluded from every donor-countable figure above. Nothing in /home/user/ktebli was modified and no production system was touched.
